paper_metadata.title: Risk of recurrence after a first seizure and implications for driving: further analysis of the Multicentre study of early Epilepsy and Single Seizures

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a detailed description of the source population and recruitment methods from the MESS trial. However, the authors explicitly acknowledge a potential selection bias because participants were only included if both the clinician and patient were 'uncertain' about starting treatment, likely excluding those at the extreme ends of the risk spectrum.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: People entered MESS if they had had one or more unprovoked seizures and both the participant and the clinician were uncertain about the need to start antiepileptic drug treatment.
items.reasoning: The target population (first unprovoked seizure) and the specific clinical context (uncertainty of treatment) are clearly defined.

items.reasoning: The recruitment setting and the use of a randomized trial framework are well-documented.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: patients were eligible for inclusion if they were at least one month old; had had at least one clinically definite, spontaneous, unprovoked epileptic seizure... Exclusion criteria included previous treatment with antiepileptic drugs or the presence of a progressive neurological disease.
items.reasoning: Detailed inclusion and exclusion criteria are listed, including the 'zero time' (index seizure).

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.evidence_snippet: Consent was not obtained for 404 of 1847 eligible patients.
items.reasoning: While the participation rate is high (~78%), the authors note that the 'uncertainty' requirement may have excluded high-risk or low-risk patients, potentially biasing the sample.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure recurrence) relies on patient self-reporting. The authors explicitly acknowledge that under-reporting is a risk, especially in a driving context where patients have an incentive to hide seizures.

items.evidence_snippet: The outcome of interest was the probability of being seizure-free for the next 12 months having been seizure-free from the index seizure to the time point in question.
items.reasoning: The outcome is clearly defined as a 12-month seizure-free interval.

items.evidence_snippet: seizures are reported to the clinician by the patient and it is possible that patients under-report the occurrence of seizures.
items.reasoning: Self-reporting is the standard but carries a risk of recall or intentional bias.
